aboutStory:
Built the same way as the Singapore guide — researched remotely using public GPS data, race reports, and Wikipedia, not walked in person.

The Las Vegas Strip Circuit is brand new (first raced in 2023), runs down public Las Vegas Boulevard and Koval Lane, and is only closed to normal traffic race week — corner positions here are a first draft and still need a proper alignment pass against the real track.

Treat it as a work in progress rather than ground truth, and if you walk it yourself, corrections and reports are very welcome.
helpSubtitle: Fan-made walking guide — S/F line + all 17 corners of the Las Vegas Strip Circuit
helpOfflineNote: After first load, the app and map tiles work fully offline. This makes it useful as a general Las Vegas Strip GPS map even when roaming doesn't work.
quirkTitle: A circuit built on the Strip itself
quirkBody: Unlike Monaco or Baku, the Las Vegas Strip Circuit runs down Las Vegas Boulevard and Koval Lane — public roads that stay open to normal traffic and pedestrians all year, closing only for a few days around the race. Corner positions in this app are a first draft based on public race reports — treat exact placements as provisional for now.
welcomeSub: Walk all 17 corners of the Las Vegas Strip Circuit, past the Sphere, Bellagio, and Caesars Palace.
welcomeSteps: Start at the S/F marker on Koval Lane — that's where the race starts and ends each lap.
Enable GPS and the app follows you — auto-advancing to the next corner as you approach. Orange markers mean you're close. Use Auto to toggle this.
Works offline — once loaded, the map and app work without internet. Useful as a general Las Vegas Strip GPS map if roaming doesn't work.
Tap Help anytime for full details on all features.
